title: Authentication vs Authorization
learningObjectives: Explain the core ideas and terminology of authentication vs authorization.
Recognize the risks or mistakes this topic is intended to prevent.
Apply appropriate defensive practices in a beginner project.
Distinguish this topic from related security concepts and controls.
Review a simple design and justify improvements using evidence.

understand.concept: Authentication establishes who or what a requester is; authorization determines which actions that identity may perform on a particular resource. A successful login does not mean every operation is permitted. Authorization checks should be enforced on the server or trusted service, using resource ownership, roles, policies, and current state—not only hidden buttons in the interface.
understand.whyItMatters: Separating identity from permission prevents a common design error: treating a logged-in user as automatically entitled to every resource.
understand.analogy: Think of a careful community space where entry, use of shared items, and privacy are guided by clear rules and appropriate checks.
understand.analogyLimit: Software security depends on technical boundaries, data flows, implementation details, and changing threats that this analogy cannot fully represent.

explain.narrative:
Authentication establishes who or what a requester is; authorization determines which actions that identity may perform on a particular resource. A successful login does not mean every operation is permitted. Authorization checks should be enforced on the server or trusted service, using resource ownership, roles, policies, and current state—not only hidden buttons in the interface.

Apply these principles proportionately. Use established platform and library protections instead of improvising security-critical mechanisms. For a real application, confirm requirements and review the implementation with qualified peers.

commonMistakes: Assuming a feature is safe because it works in normal use.
Trusting client-side controls as the only enforcement.
Applying one generic transformation to every kind of input or output.
Exposing credentials or personal data in source, logs, or screenshots.

independentTask.title: Independent Practice
independentTask.instructions: Build a permission matrix for a fictional library app. Include read, create, update, and delete for two roles. Explain how authentication and authorization are checked separately on server routes.
requirements: Use a fictional or toy project and no real secrets or personal data.
Build a permission matrix for a fictional library app. Include read, create, update, and delete for two roles. Explain how authentication and authorization are checked separately on server routes.

questions.prompt: Is a logged-in user automatically allowed to delete any record?
options: No; permission must be checked for that resource and action
Only if the button is visible
Yes, if their browser is modern
questions.answer: No; permission must be checked for that resource and action
questions.explanation: Authentication does not grant unrestricted authorization.

questions.prompt: Where should important authorization checks be enforced?
options: On the trusted backend or service
questions.answer: On the trusted backend or service

questions.prompt: What is a sensible default when permission is unknown?
questions.explanation: Failing closed protects access when checks cannot be established.
